name: water-leaper

attributes.attribute: a kind of giant leaping toad
the Welsh name for the water-leaper
hides in the water until a man or beast passes
drags victims underwater to eat them

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The water-leaper is a monster of Welsh legend. Welsh people call it the llamhigyn y dwr. In habit it stands with the Water Bull and the Water Horse. The beast has the shape of a giant leaping toad. It lies well hidden in the water. When a man or a beast comes near, the monster leaps out. It grabs the prey with a sudden grip. Then it drags the victim below and eats the catch underwater.

okr.objective: The water-leaper is a Welsh creature that seizes its prey at the edge of the water.
key_results: The llamhigyn y dwr is the Welsh name for the beast.
The water-leaper has the shape of a giant toad.
It hides in water until a man or animal passes near.
Then it leaps out and drags the victim below to eat the prey.
